newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper to range, aluminium struggle.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper to range, aluminium struggle.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices are likely to end the week still ranging, unable to clear $2,600 overhead at present, analysts said.
Aluminium meanwhile is seen struggling after failing consistently at $1,600, and may test $1,565, they said.
Trading activity was mostly subdued on Thursday, which suggests a tired market will probably remain within a $2,570 to $2,600 band.
"Technically, prices remain rangebound still, with a break-out of the $2,560/70 - $2,600/10 band awaited to give fresh direction," LME trader Brandeis said in its daily report.

"This market still appears to be consolidating before breaking higher. However, $2,570 remains important support and if broken falls to $2,550 and lower could be seen," Harry Creates of LME trader Amalgamated Metal Trading said.
Meanwhile, some attention was being paid to the Inco dispute in Canada, where latest news indicated the strike may drag on through the summer maintenance shutdown period.
At 0736 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,576/80, down around $6 from Thursday's late close.
Traders expect the aluminium market to do little in the short-term, given the sluggish performances when prices approach $1,600.
"It is still very much range-bound between $1,560/1,620, with an inner range of $1,580/1,610," one trader said.
"The market struggles to find direction, still attracting support on dips, but finding good scale-up selling interest up above," Christopher Hill of LME trader Gerald Ltd said.
Brandeis noted that the close on Thursday was disappointing and highlighted downside support, initially at $1,560/65, then $1,550 and $1,530.
Later on Friday, IPAI May production data could provide some interest, with output expected little changed to slightly down, analysts said.
At 0736 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,581/84, down slightly from the previous late close of $1,583/85. --Martin Hayes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8080
